entities.label: Lucasfilm's Habitat

milestones.what: beta opens on Quantum Link for the Commodore 64

entities.blurb: The 1986 Commodore 64 world that invented the graphical avatar, the online economy, and most of the problems every virtual world has faced since.

entities.label: Club Caribe
entities.blurb: Habitat scaled down to a virtual island resort so Quantum Link could actually afford to run it, surviving until the Commodore service itself died.

entities.label: Fujitsu Habitat

milestones.what: launches on NIFTY-Serve in Japan, passing 1,000 citizens within months

entities.blurb: Lucasfilm's Habitat licensed to Fujitsu and reborn in Japan, where it quietly outlived its American parent by well over a decade.

entities.label: WorldsAway

milestones.what: Fujitsu sells it off; it lives on as VZones
the last VZones worlds close in August

entities.blurb: Fujitsu's CompuServe-era Dreamscape, a direct Habitat descendant where avatars could literally carry their heads in their hands.

entities.label: The Palace

milestones.what: folded into the Softbank-backed Electric Communities/Communities.com group
official development dies with Communities.com's bankruptcy; fan servers carry on

entities.blurb: Jim Bumgardner's 2D avatar chat of painted rooms and floating prop-heads, the counterculture living room of the 1995 internet.

entities.label: Worlds Chat

milestones.what: Worlds Chat Gold ships as a retail CD-ROM

entities.blurb: The April 1995 space-station chat world that beat everyone to 3D avatars, and whose ghost servers still accept the occasional visitor.

entities.label: AlphaWorld / Active Worlds

milestones.what: renamed Active Worlds under new owner Circle of Fire / Activeworlds Inc

entities.blurb: Ron Britvich's June 1995 frontier where users could claim land and build, creating the first sprawling citizen-built virtual city years before Second Life.

entities.label: Cybertown

milestones.what: subscription fees begin the long decline
former citizens launch a community revival

entities.blurb: A VRML sci-fi city with jobs, houses, and civic ranks that grew past a million registered citizens before going dark in 2012.

entities.label: OZ Virtual

milestones.what: tech spun off as SmartVR; the team's lineage feeds into CCP and EVE Online

entities.blurb: OZ Interactive's stylish VRML world of motion-captured dancing avatars whose Icelandic alumni went on to seed EVE Online.

entities.label: OnLive! Traveler

milestones.what: rescued by Bruce Damer's DigitalSpace as Digital Space Traveler

entities.blurb: Floating heads with real-time voice and lip-sync in 1996 — spatial voice chat a full two decades before social VR made it table stakes.

entities.label: Sony Community Place

milestones.what: world's first VRML 2.0 browser released free
the SAPARi service closes in January

entities.blurb: Sony's VRML chat system, preloaded on VAIO laptops as SAPARi, that co-wrote the Moving Worlds proposal behind VRML 2.0.

entities.label: There

milestones.what: closes March 9 as the recession guts revenue
relaunches as a subscription service for adults

entities.blurb: The polished, PG-rated hoverboard-and-buggy world that fought Second Life for the future of avatar socializing and lost gracefully — twice.

entities.label: Second Life

milestones.what: mainstream hype peak: real companies and a virtual millionaire

entities.blurb: Linden Lab's user-built universe with a real-money economy that became the household synonym for 'virtual world' and simply never died.

entities.label: OpenSimulator

milestones.what: Hypergrid links independent grids into a federated metaverse

entities.blurb: The open-source reimplementation of Second Life's server that let anyone run their own grid and federate it with strangers.

entities.label: IMVU
entities.blurb: Room-by-room avatar chat with a massive user-generated catalog, and the startup whose pivots gave Eric Ries the Lean Startup gospel.

entities.label: Habbo Hotel
entities.blurb: Sulake's pixelated Finnish hotel that checked in hundreds of millions of teenagers and taught them what a furni economy was.

entities.label: Club Penguin

milestones.what: Disney buys it for up to $700M
shut down in March; fan clones later forced offline too

entities.blurb: The waddling penguin world that became an entire generation's first online society before Disney iced it in 2017.

entities.label: Toontown Online

milestones.what: fans resurrect it as Toontown Rewritten

entities.blurb: Disney's kid-safe MMO where cartoon citizens fought humorless corporate robots — closed in 2013, resurrected by its own fans.

entities.label: Gaia Online
entities.blurb: The anime-flavored forum-plus-avatar community that was one of the web's biggest teen hangouts of the mid-2000s.

entities.label: PlayStation Home

milestones.what: closed worldwide March 31 after 41 million users

entities.blurb: Sony's console-bound virtual plaza where PS3 owners queued their avatars for bowling — mocked constantly, mourned genuinely.

entities.label: Blue Mars

milestones.what: PC development ceases; company pivots to iOS
technology handed to Ball State University

entities.blurb: A CryEngine-powered, Hawaii-built bid to out-render Second Life on a terraformed Mars that ran out of oxygen by 2012.

entities.label: Twinity

milestones.what: acquired by ExitReality
servers taken offline in December

entities.blurb: Metaversum's mirror-world that rebuilt real Berlin, Singapore, and London to scale so your avatar could live at your actual address.

entities.label: Entropia Universe

milestones.what: virtual asteroid sells for a record $100,000 real dollars

entities.blurb: MindArk's sci-fi world with a fixed dollar exchange rate, where virtual real estate deals kept setting real-world Guinness records.

entities.label: Virtual World of Kaneva

milestones.what: world shut down November 14

entities.blurb: An Atlanta-built world that fused social networking profiles with 3D hangouts a beat too early, closing quietly in 2016.

entities.label: Cloud Party

milestones.what: team acqui-hired by Yahoo in February; world closed

entities.blurb: A no-download, WebGL virtual world that ran inside a browser tab — and even inside Facebook — years before that was normal.

entities.label: JanusVR

milestones.what: company founded by James McCrae and Karan Singh
company winds down; code open-sourced and continued by the community

entities.blurb: A browser that reimagined the web itself as connected 3D rooms, where hyperlinks became doorways you walk through.

entities.label: Mozilla Hubs

milestones.what: Mozilla shuts it down May 31; Hubs Foundation inherits the code

entities.blurb: Mozilla's open-source WebXR meeting rooms that ran in any browser and hosted nearly ten million visitors before the 2024 shutdown.

entities.label: Cryptovoxels / Voxels

milestones.what: renamed Voxels

entities.blurb: Ben Nolan's browser-based voxel city on the Ethereum blockchain, the scrappy indie corner of the NFT land rush.

entities.label: Decentraland

milestones.what: public launch in February
virtual land parcels sell for millions in the metaverse boom

entities.blurb: The DAO-governed crypto world whose land deeds sold for millions at the boom's peak while its plazas often sat eerily empty.

entities.label: Somnium Space
entities.blurb: A VR-first blockchain world of persistent land and full-body avatars, best known for its founder's dream of 'live forever' avatar preservation.

entities.label: The Sandbox

milestones.what: public alpha rides the metaverse boom; Snoop Dogg buys in

entities.blurb: Animoca's voxel metaverse where celebrities and brands bought LAND tokens, the maximalist face of the crypto land grab.

entities.label: AltspaceVR

milestones.what: near-death shutdown reversed by Microsoft acquisition in October
Microsoft closes it March 10, folding the team into Mesh

entities.blurb: The friendly front porch of early consumer VR — comedy nights and meetups — saved once by Microsoft and later killed by it.

entities.label: High Fidelity

milestones.what: abandons its open-source VR world platform
relaunches as a spatial-audio company

entities.blurb: Philip Rosedale's open-source, decentralized do-over of Second Life for VR that arrived before the headsets did, then pivoted to selling its spatial audio.

entities.label: Sansar

milestones.what: Linden Lab sells it to Wookey Project Corp in March

entities.blurb: Linden Lab's 'WordPress for VR' successor bid that never inherited Second Life's crowds and was sold off so Linden could go home again.

entities.label: VRChat

milestones.what: Steam Early Access opens the floodgates in February
goes viral, exploding to millions of users

entities.blurb: The anything-goes universe of user-built worlds and avatars that became social VR's chaotic capital city and its longest-running success.

entities.label: Rec Room

milestones.what: reaches unicorn status on the back of cross-platform play

entities.blurb: The summer-camp of social VR — paintball, quests, and player-built rooms — that outgrew headsets entirely by going cross-platform.

entities.label: Bigscreen

milestones.what: ships the ultralight Bigscreen Beyond headset

entities.blurb: The virtual living room where strangers watch movies together, whose maker then shipped one of the lightest VR headsets ever built.

entities.label: Neos VR

milestones.what: development team departs after the Solirax split; platform left frozen

entities.blurb: Frooxius's astonishing build-everything-in-headset engine where the world editor, avatars, and even the UI were live objects you could grab.

entities.label: Resonite

milestones.what: launches October 6 and the Neos community migrates en masse

entities.blurb: The clean-slate rebuild Frooxius made after splitting with Neos's publisher, carrying his community and in-world-everything philosophy with him.

entities.label: Horizon Worlds

milestones.what: invite-only beta opens
a legless avatar selfie becomes the metaverse era's defining meme

entities.blurb: Meta's flagship social world, launched with the weight of a corporate rename behind it and forever haunted by one legless screenshot.

entities.label: Facebook Spaces

milestones.what: shut down October 25 as Horizon is announced

entities.blurb: Facebook's cartoon-avatar VR hangout for your real friends list, retired after two years to clear the stage for Horizon.

entities.label: Lucasfilm Games
entities.blurb: George Lucas's game studio, which bankrolled the improbable experiment that became the first graphical virtual world.

entities.label: Fujitsu
entities.blurb: The Japanese electronics giant that kept the Habitat bloodline alive across two continents long after Lucasfilm moved on.

entities.label: Electric Communities

milestones.what: renamed Communities.com after absorbing The Palace
bankruptcy ends official Palace development

entities.blurb: The Habitat veterans' deeply ambitious attempt to build a secure, decentralized metaverse in the 1990s, whose E language outlived its worlds.

entities.label: Worlds Inc

milestones.what: ships both Worlds Chat and AlphaWorld within months
resurfaces as a patent litigant against game giants

entities.blurb: The company that launched two founding 3D worlds in one year, then spent its afterlife suing the industry over metaverse patents.

entities.label: Activeworlds Inc
entities.blurb: The small operation that bought Active Worlds from Worlds Inc in 1997 and has kept the pioneer world's servers humming ever since.

entities.label: blaxxun interactive

milestones.what: renames from Black Sun Interactive — both names lifted from Snow Crash
insolvency ends the original company

entities.blurb: The Munich VRML pioneer literally named after Snow Crash's metaverse bar, whose multi-user tech powered Cybertown.

entities.label: Linden Lab
entities.blurb: Philip Rosedale's San Francisco lab that turned a haptics experiment into Second Life and has stewarded it for over two decades.

entities.label: The Walt Disney Company
entities.blurb: The entertainment empire that built Toontown, bought Club Penguin, and eventually shuttered both kid-world experiments.

entities.label: Sony
entities.blurb: Twice a virtual-world builder: VRML's Community Place in the 90s and the PS3's PlayStation Home a decade later.

entities.label: Microsoft

milestones.what: acquires AltspaceVR
shuts AltspaceVR, folding social VR into Mesh

entities.blurb: The giant that rescued AltspaceVR in 2017, then retired it in 2023 in favor of enterprise-flavored Mesh.

entities.label: Meta

milestones.what: buys Oculus for $2 billion
renames from Facebook, betting the company on the metaverse

entities.blurb: The social network that renamed itself after the metaverse and spent tens of billions trying to build one people would visit.

entities.label: Mozilla
entities.blurb: The open-web foundation whose Hubs proved browser-native social VR worked, then handed the keys to its community in 2024.

entities.label: Chip Morningstar
entities.blurb: Habitat's lead designer, whose 'Lessons of Lucasfilm's Habitat' paper became the founding document of virtual-world design.

entities.label: Randy Farmer
entities.blurb: Habitat's co-creator and the field's institutional memory, still dispensing avatar-economy wisdom four decades on.

entities.label: Jim Bumgardner
entities.blurb: The programmer-artist who built The Palace and gave 90s internet culture its prop-wearing floating heads.

entities.label: Ron Britvich
entities.blurb: The engineer who single-handedly prototyped AlphaWorld and handed ordinary users the power to build a virtual continent.

entities.label: Bruce Damer

milestones.what: publishes Avatars!, the field's first survey book

entities.blurb: The chronicler and evangelist of the first avatar era, who founded the Contact Consortium and kept Traveler alive through DigitalSpace.

entities.label: Philip Rosedale

milestones.what: returns to Second Life as strategic advisor

entities.blurb: The metaverse's most persistent believer, who built Second Life, tried again with High Fidelity, and came back to Second Life anyway.

entities.label: Will Harvey
entities.blurb: The teenage game-dev prodigy who founded There and then IMVU, betting twice that avatars were the future of hanging out.

entities.label: Graham Gaylor
entities.blurb: VRChat's founder, who started with a tiny DK1 chat demo and ended up mayor of social VR's biggest city.

entities.label: Jesse Joudrey
entities.blurb: VRChat's co-founder and CTO, the engineering half of the pair that scaled a hobby chat app into a platform of millions.

entities.label: Tomáš "Frooxius" Mariančík
entities.blurb: The Czech engine wizard who essentially solo-built Neos VR, then rebuilt his entire vision as Resonite after splitting with his publisher.

entities.label: James McCrae
entities.blurb: The University of Toronto graphics PhD who decided web links should be doors and built JanusVR to prove it.
